displayContract.byline: Assessments made by 5.6 Sol. — Rubric: Slugfester Reassessment Rubric v2.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that a necessary mental foundation merits preference only if a compact generative structure explains otherwise independent modal, axiological, causal, and phenomenal facts better than plural foundations do.

novelty.explanation: This replaces a compressed unlimitedness inference with a comparative generative criterion spanning the principal theistic moves.

premises.text: Explanatory simplicity concerns total generative commitments, not merely the number of primitive words, so a unified foundation is advantageous only when its derivations reduce overall independent structure.

novelty.explanation: This repairs the missing criterion connecting primitive economy and axiomatic analogy to whole-theory simplicity.

premises.text: Attributes such as knowledge, agency, and value should be derived through independently defended functional requirements for comprehensive explanation, rather than inferred immediately from an unrestricted scalar magnitude.

novelty.explanation: This directly corrects the exposed transition from removing limits to positive mental and personal structure.

premises.text: Phenomenal consciousness supports a mental foundation only insofar as specified features resist available physical identity accounts and become more expected under the proposed foundational model.

novelty.explanation: This supplies the comparative likelihood requirement missing from the live introspective compatibility argument.

premises.text: Accepting token identity between a conscious episode and neural processing remains compatible with irreducible phenomenal properties, but that compatibility alone does not determine their ultimate metaphysical ground.

novelty.explanation: This develops the careful token-type distinction while preserving its appropriately limited argumentative consequence.

premises.text: Every local advantage must be integrated with suffering, divine hiddenness, physical regularity, modal structure, and rival explanatory costs before supporting a complete-worldview preference.

novelty.explanation: This completes the integration step that Rasmussen acknowledged but did not operationalize in the selected exchange.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, theism gains a proportionate comparative advantage only if its mental foundation supplies defensible cross-domain derivations and consciousness predictions whose total compression exceeds the costs of its additional structure.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion narrows the theistic claim to the comparative success conditions established by the repaired premises.

newArguments.title: Invariance-based compression test
newArguments.text: A unified foundation should be evaluated by whether the same small set of structural principles generates explanations across importantly different domains without domain-specific amendments. If mentality, value, modality, and causal power each require separate auxiliary assumptions, the advertised unification is largely verbal. If one independently motivated architecture constrains all four and yields counterfactual expectations that plural foundations do not, the resulting invariance supplies a measurable form of explanatory compression. This test strengthens the theistic route while exposing it to a demanding comparison rather than treating unity itself as automatically advantageous.

novelty.explanation: This is a new methodological test using cross-domain invariance to distinguish substantive unification from merely verbal consolidation.

newArguments.title: Phenomenal bridge profile
newArguments.text: Instead of arguing from consciousness in general, the theistic case could identify a profile of features requiring joint explanation: first-person accessibility, unified subjecthood, intentional content, rational responsiveness, and causal integration with neural activity. It could then compare how strongly a foundational mind and neural identity predict that conjunction, including their respective auxiliary commitments. A comparative profile avoids relying on introspection alone and prevents mere compatibility from masquerading as evidence. The argument succeeds only if the mental-foundation model assigns the conjunction a better-supported expectation without adding equally complex bridge principles.

novelty.explanation: This strengthens the consciousness route by replacing a generic compatibility claim with a specified comparative evidence profile.

thesis.text: The AI steelman is that naturalism should prefer a necessary physical initial reality only when disciplined pluralism and neural explanation outperform theism across total commitments without presuming that physical continuity settles every domain.

novelty.explanation: This integrates Oppy's strongest lines while correcting the risk that continuity or pluralism might be treated as self-justifying.

premises.text: The initial reality should receive no positive attribute beyond what explanatory and empirical considerations warrant, so nonmentality is a provisional model commitment rather than an automatic consequence of simplicity.

novelty.explanation: This preserves epistemic restraint while avoiding an unsupported inference from rejecting theism to asserting nonmentality.

premises.text: Independent necessary domains are acceptable only when their separate structures and interrelations produce lower total theoretical cost than the bridge principles required by a single common foundation.

novelty.explanation: This supplies the missing comparative cost criterion for the plural-foundations proposal.

premises.text: Neural identity requires positive support from systematic dependence, intervention, lesion, development, and representational organization, not merely the observation that introspection cannot disprove identity.

novelty.explanation: This adds the affirmative evidential burden left open by the successful epistemic rebuttal.

premises.text: A physical account must explain why content-bearing processing constitutes phenomenal availability and unified subjecthood rather than merely correlating with them under ordinary neurological conditions.

novelty.explanation: This addresses the unresolved phenomenal-exhaustion problem identified in the content-processing reply.

premises.text: Whole-worldview comparison must evaluate naturalistic and theistic auxiliary commitments symmetrically, including unexplained laws, consciousness, value, suffering, hiddenness, regularity, and modal structure.

novelty.explanation: This develops the methodological standard into a concrete symmetry requirement across relevant evidence classes.

conclusion.text: Accordingly, naturalism earns a proportionate preference only if its costed pluralism and positive neural account explain the total evidence with fewer unsupported bridges than the proposed supreme mental foundation.

novelty.explanation: The conclusion makes naturalistic preference conditional on satisfying the strengthened explanatory and comparative burdens.

newArguments.title: Modular dependence test
newArguments.text: Plural foundations need not be treated as unrelated brute facts if their independence is tested through modular counterfactual dependence. Logic, value, physical law, and consciousness may require different explanatory kinds when alterations in one domain neither determine nor coherently vary the others. A modular model can then compare the cost of several constrained foundations against a single foundation plus multiple heterogeneous bridge principles. This framework gives naturalistic pluralism a positive architecture while conceding that multiplication is costly whenever the proposed modules lack principled boundaries or require extensive coordination assumptions.

novelty.explanation: This introduces a new counterfactual method for determining when plural foundations are principled rather than merely accumulated.

newArguments.title: Intervention-based identity ladder
newArguments.text: The neural identity case can be strengthened through an evidential ladder: correlation locates candidate processes, selective intervention tests causal necessity and sufficiency, representational analysis explains content, and cross-subject structural regularities test whether the same organization predicts reported phenomenal distinctions. None of these steps alone establishes identity, but their convergence can make identity more economical than a dual-property account requiring additional psychophysical laws. The comparison must still confront inverted or absent phenomenal qualities and explain unified subjecthood; those challenges become explicit model-selection tests rather than conclusions derived solely from introspective ignorance.

novelty.explanation: This supplies the positive empirical program required to extend the transcript's mainly diagnostic defense of neural identity.
